name: Recipes and meal planning
intro: Where recipes save from the web and the shopping list builds itself, and where your collection just vanishes.

apps.title: AnyList: Grocery Shopping List
apps.verdict: One of the best tools for grocery list management and recipe organization in the category. Family sync is reliable, URL recipe import works, and Apple Watch support is genuinely useful at the store. The missing pieces are store checkout integration and an open API for third-party developers.
apps.loved: Instant grocery list sync across all family members has worked reliably for years.
apps.weak: No budget tracking inside the list and no open API for integrations.
apps.whoFor: Families and couples who maintain a shared grocery list and store recipes in one place

quotes.text: AnyList has been incredible and I've used for many years with my spouse. Watch app is great, syncing is solid, and instacart integration is awesome. Highly recommend.

This is a great app for planning meal and automatically adding the ingredients to your shopping list. The only downside is that I would like to be able to track my spending as I am going through the store by barcoding the prices.

apps.title: NYT Cooking: Quick Tasty Meals
apps.verdict: An editorial recipe library from the New York Times with thousands of tested recipes and a strong community. The main complaint is that forced app updates cut off users on older devices, and search within saved recipes is clunky.
apps.loved: A vast and varied recipe base from professional culinary editors you can actually trust.
apps.weak: Saved recipes cannot be organized into folders and are hard to find in a long, unstructured list.
apps.whoFor: People who want editorially vetted recipes rather than a planner or tracker

quotes.text: Pay for subscription and get huge adds on all recipes. If your app accidentally closes and you're in the middle of a recipe, good luck when you open it back up you might not find that recipe. There's no way to lock the page or find it again. That waste a lot of money and time when food is wasted.
Recipes on the NYT email links are always interesting. I have SAVED numerous ones but when I go to the recipe box it is often difficult to locate my saved personal folders and recipes.
I have used this app since the first day it was introduced. It is a fabulous resource for recipes. However, the search function is archaic. It just doesn't work well in any wa...

apps.title: Umami - Recipe Manager
apps.verdict: One of the best recipe managers with fast URL import and a convenient shopping list built from selected dishes. The weak spot is unstable import from Instagram and NYT, which frustrates active users on a regular basis.
apps.loved: URL-based recipe import works quickly and accurately; a shopping list is ready in seconds.
apps.weak: Import from Instagram and some major publications breaks after platform updates.
apps.whoFor: People who collect recipes from the web and want one tidy place for them

apps.title: Paprika Recipe Manager 3
apps.verdict: Paprika remains the best personal recipe archive: web import works as expected, there is a planner and shopping list, and data is well structured. The main pain in recent months is that the built-in browser has become unstable and stopped downloading recipes for some users.
apps.loved: Instant import of any recipe from the web, stripped of ads and filler text.
apps.weak: The built-in browser periodically breaks and fails to load recipes, and the app has gone a long time without updates.
apps.whoFor: People who build a personal recipe collection from multiple sources

quotes.text: Really liked the app until I went to import a recipe from Instagram and can't. Surprised they don't support that feature. Recipe keeper does.
I seriously would be so lost without this app! Been using it for several years. We use all of the features…calendar, grocery list, sharing it the family, categorizing recipes, etc.

Brilliant for capturing recipes from websites. It should be made much easier to schedule a recipe (on rolling calendar date spinner) in fewer clicks and to reschedule a recipe to tomorrow or another night when my cooking plans change.

apps.title: Crouton: Recipe Manager
apps.verdict: One of the best recipe managers on iOS: smart URL import, step-by-step cooking mode, family sharing, and a clean design. Recipe ratings and calendar integration are still missing, and bulk import from PDF is slow.
apps.loved: Importing a recipe from Instagram, a website, or a photo at a friend's kitchen takes a few seconds.
apps.weak: No way to rate individual recipes, making it hard to find proven favorites in a large collection.
apps.whoFor: Passionate home cooks who want a single recipe organizer with family sharing

apps.title: America's Test Kitchen
apps.verdict: America's Test Kitchen delivers meticulously developed recipes with video and notes — the strongest content in the category. The downsides are purely technical: the app occasionally fails to open, saved recipe sorting is absent, and there is no meal planner.
apps.loved: Recipes are tested repeatedly until the result is perfect, with video and user notes on every dish.
apps.weak: No meal planner and no way to copy an ingredient list directly from a recipe.
apps.whoFor: Serious home cooks who care about recipe reliability above all else

quotes.text: It would be extremely helpful for users to be able to sort ones favorites alphabetically, online and in the app, especially when adding a recipe or article to favorites. Currently it's a tedious task to scroll through the favorites list to find a category.
I'm enjoying this app and the recipes are pretty good so far. I'd really like to see a meal planning option where I could save recipes for the days of the week.
If you have a random ingredient and wonder what to do with it, the search feature will give you lots of options. Clear instructions and many of the recipes also have videos.

apps.title: Recipe Keeper - OrganizEat
apps.verdict: One of the best personal recipe organizers with photo import, OCR, and a simple day-by-day planner. A small rate of data loss and occasional AI extraction failures do not outweigh its overall reliability.
apps.loved: A photo of a cookbook or magazine page turns into a structured recipe with a title and ingredient list in seconds.
apps.weak: AI import sometimes drops or substitutes ingredients, so the recipe needs a manual check before the first cook.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to gather family recipes and web finds in one place

quotes.text: No warning whatsoever. Just suddenly gone and irretrievable!!! Don't use this app as you could lose everything without warning!!!

apps.title: Deglaze: Cooking, Simplified
apps.verdict: One of the best tools for importing recipes from blogs and social media: X-ray mode strips out advertising noise and leaves only the recipe, and cooking mode keeps the screen on. Serving scaling was moved behind a paywall, which frustrates longtime users.
apps.loved: X-ray mode removes all blog text and leaves only ingredients and steps; the screen stays on while you cook.
apps.weak: Serving scaling became a paid feature despite requiring no server-side processing.
apps.whoFor: Active home cooks who collect recipes from websites and social media

quotes.text: Use X-ray mode to view just the actual recipe and "start cooking" to activate recipe mode so your phone doesn't lock while you are cooking. Does a good job of pulling the actual recipe from lengthy blog posts, that's my favorite part!

When I first got the app I loved how much it could do especially with the language support and scaling for a lot of my non-English recipes. The new update decided to make scaling for members only, which is a basic function that other recipe apps still have for free!

apps.title: Copy Me That recipe manager
apps.verdict: One of the best tools for saving recipes from web pages in one click: it strips ads and filler text, supports tags, filters, and a menu planner. The main complaints are about the shift to a paid model rather than product problems.
apps.loved: Instant recipe saving from any website without copy-pasting or ad clutter.
apps.weak: Recipes from Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube cannot be imported directly.
apps.whoFor: Active collectors of recipes from web pages and cooking blogs

apps.title: Daily Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A minimal planner with no excess: enter dish names, assign them to days, share with a partner. A widget, automatic shopping list, and notifications are missing, but the core mechanic works reliably.
apps.loved: Simple weekly view, full meal history, and the ability to share the plan with a partner.
apps.weak: The shopping list is not generated automatically from the plan, and there is no home screen widget.
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple weekly meal plan without recipes or extra complexity

apps.title: Pestle: Recipe Manager
apps.verdict: One of the best recipe managers for import quality and interface design. Family access and nested recipes set it apart from competitors, but the meal planner is weak.
apps.loved: Smart URL import, recipes nested inside each other, and a clean native interface.
apps.weak: The meal planner has no breakfast, lunch, and dinner breakdown, which limits its practical use.
apps.whoFor: People who want to organize a recipe collection beautifully and add new ones easily

apps.title: Calorie Counter - MyNetDiary
apps.verdict: A calorie and nutrition tracker with an extensive food database, recipe import, and smart device integration. It handles basic logging well and helps users reach weight goals, but the interface has slowed down and navigation between sections is unnecessarily tangled.
apps.loved: A huge food database and the ability to save custom meals make daily logging fast.
apps.weak: Recipe import is awkward and poorly documented despite the claimed support.
apps.whoFor: People who want accurate macro tracking without extra subscriptions or gamification

quotes.text: I like that we can import recipes, however, it's very cumbersome and not easy as stated in the instructions.

apps.title: Mela - Recipe Manager
apps.verdict: A beautiful native recipe collection app with excellent web import, a menu planner, and no subscription. The main issue is that the developer does not respond to support requests and has not updated the app in over a year, and recipe sharing between different iCloud accounts does not work.
apps.loved: One-time purchase with no subscription, a polished design, and reliable recipe import from websites.
apps.weak: Search requires scrolling all the way to the top of the list, which is frustrating with a collection of thousands of recipes.
apps.whoFor: Someone with a large personal recipe collection who values design and does not want a monthly fee

apps.title: Recipe Keeper
apps.verdict: Recipe Keeper handles manual entry, web import, and recipe scanning well, and includes a meal planner and shopping list generation. The main limitation is that family sharing requires separate purchases on every device and platform, which makes shared kitchen management inconvenient.
apps.loved: Fast recipe import via URL, page scanning, or manual entry into a single archive.
apps.weak: No shared family access: each person must buy the app separately on every platform they use.
apps.whoFor: Home cooks who want to keep a personal recipe archive in one place

quotes.text: The Pros: Easy to use. Multiple methods of adding new recipes. Menu planner that creates a shopping list. THE CONS: The shopping list doesn't export to grocery store apps. SPOUSE CANNOT ACCESS THE MENU, RECIPES, SHOPPING LIST, ETC. We cannot sync between our two apple accounts.
I like everything about this, but it needs to be able to double a recipe, or half a recipe.

apps.title: Recipe Keeper - Cook'n
apps.verdict: A mature recipe storage and organization tool with solid URL import and cross-device sync. Paper recipe scanning is inaccurate, and occasional data loss when switching phones undermines trust.
apps.loved: Years of accumulated recipes with URL import, accessible from phone, tablet, and laptop.
apps.weak: Scanning and recognizing printed recipes works noticeably worse than in competing apps.
apps.whoFor: Home cooks with a large personal recipe archive who want to digitize and sync it

quotes.text: I have lost all my recipes after the launch/reboot issue the app just had. I have been storing these for years and now some of our family favorite recipes are gone. This is the worst app ever!

apps.title: Ollie for Meals: Meal Planning
apps.verdict: An AI meal planner that genuinely takes over weekly meal selection based on dietary constraints and automatically builds a shopping list. The list occasionally misses ingredients and the AI can be repetitive, but the concept works and saves time.
apps.loved: Automatic weekly meal plan tailored to family dietary needs plus a ready shopping list with no manual work.
apps.weak: The shopping list sometimes drops ingredients, and old items are not cleared between weeks automatically.
apps.whoFor: A busy parent or anyone who does not have time to decide what to cook

apps.title: FitMenCook - Healthy Recipes
apps.verdict: FitMenCook is a solid collection of fitness-oriented recipes with video and a shopping list. But the meal planner is poorly implemented, allergen filtering is absent, and some recipes depend on the brand's proprietary spice blends.
apps.loved: Recipes taste good and fit a fitness routine; new ones are added on a regular basis.
apps.weak: No allergen filter and the meal planning feature is not in a working state.
apps.whoFor: People in an active training routine who want quick, satisfying recipes

quotes.text: There is no option or setting to filter out specific foods, like dairy or nuts. This makes it not very useful for those of us with food allergies.

The lay out is great. Videos and shopping list creation is another great tool. The one thing missing is that it does give the nutritional values, but I am not finding the serving size weight. It just shows what a serving size nutrition value as far as macros without weight in grams or ounces.

apps.title: MealPrepPro Planner & Recipes
apps.verdict: Works well at automatically planning a meal-prep week with a ready shopping list. Weak points include no pantry tracking, incomplete allergen filters, and macro adjustment within a narrow range only.
apps.loved: In 30 minutes on Sunday it produces a weekly batch-cooking plan with step-by-step video and a shopping list.
apps.weak: No way to account for what is already at home, and you cannot add your own recipes to the plan.
apps.whoFor: Busy people who cook all their food for the week in one session

quotes.text: This app would be amazing and everything I wanted it to be if it had an inventory where you could tell it what you had in your pantry, fridge, and freezer and it could build your meals around what you already had and then make your grocery list for only the things you needed to buy.

I'm still in the trial period but after only one day of meal prep (10 days of recipes took 3 hours of shopping) I'm exhausted. The shopping list and the recipes tell you most things in ounces. I guess we're supposed to weigh everything. It's a real hassle.

This app has helped me keep control of my eating habits and makes it easy for a busy single mother. The only hard part is knowing how much to put in each meal prep container. A break down of this other than the video would be helpful.

apps.title: Samsung Food: Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A strong tool for recipe storage and shopping list generation, but UX quality dropped noticeably after the Samsung acquisition. Import from third-party sites still works, while ingredient accuracy and sync have run into issues.
apps.loved: Automatic shopping list generation with ingredients sorted by type, ready to use in the store.
apps.weak: Ingredient-based search does not rank recipes by how many pantry items they actually use up.
apps.whoFor: Home cooks who need to store recipes and build a shopping list quickly

quotes.text: My spouse and I use this everyday with shopping as well as meal planning of course. We love the added resource of being part of different recipe communities as well as health issues that come up.

I paid the subscription for this app mainly for one thing: the fact it can look for recipes that use up your ingredients and "reduce waste". However, whenever I search for recipes with my ingredient list, it doesn't put the recipes first that actually use up your ingredients!! It's random and only e...

The app used to organize recipes well. Now, the amounts of ingredients (esp. grams, ounces) do not match the amounts provided on the original recipe website. The weights and amounts are inconsistent to the point that the ingredients tab in the app is useless.

apps.title: ReciMe: Recipes & Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A recipe saving and organization app with URL import, serving scaling, and shopping list generation. Web import works well, but a free limit of 5 recipes cuts users off before they can properly evaluate the product.
apps.loved: One-tap URL recipe import and automatic shopping list with serving scaling.
apps.weak: Search within your own collection is poor even after paying for a subscription.
apps.whoFor: People who want to build a personal culinary library from links and social media

quotes.text: I wish it could take recipes from within the video instead of just the caption on tiktok, like how Mijo does for travel. and not nearly as important but i wish it made the thumbnail from the tiktok or a photo or something the photo in the recipe so we don't manually have to add it

ReciMe makes it easy to organize, share, and sort recipes. I appreciate the ease of increasing and decreasing portion sizes and creating grocery lists. Being able to download from anywhere the web is fantastic!

I love that I can move my favorite recipes here without retyping everything and it gives me a shopping list, but when I compare nutrition information from app to what is stated from the original site and what I create in MyFitnessPal, the numbers are way off. And they are always lower in ReciMe.

apps.title: Eat This Much - Meal Planner
apps.verdict: Eat This Much works well as an automatic meal plan generator with a shopping list and nutrient tracking. The main problem is that the recipe base gets repetitive and the vegetarian section is thin.
apps.loved: Auto-generated meal plan to match your goals, complete with a shopping list and Apple Health sync.
apps.weak: The recipe library gets old fast; the same dishes rotate every week.
apps.whoFor: People who count macros and want to automate grocery shopping

quotes.text: This app was exactly what I was looking for… automated recipe planning with automatic grocery list building based off your week, pantry management, and syncs with Apple health for tracking. My only complaint is the pantry management system could be more automated.
The app needs to let us publicly rate and review recipes. Some of the recipes are horrible. However. It is amazing for tracking calories and planning meals. The groceries list feature is the best!

My son has a lot of food allergies and eating for our family is not a fun experience. Friend recommended this because you can put the food exclusions in and it supposedly generates meals around them. But it doesn't.

I'm really losing patience with this app and about ready to request a refund. It's just one series of useless recommendations after another. The same disgusting recipes pushed over and over no matter how many times I block them.

apps.title: Just the Recipe: Cook smarter
apps.verdict: A great idea, but the recipe parser is becoming less reliable: roughly every second or third source fails to parse. Those who get lucky receive a clean recipe stripped of ads and pop-ups, which is genuinely useful at the stove.
apps.loved: Extracts the recipe from ad-heavy pages and leaves only the ingredients and instructions.
apps.weak: Manual recipe entry is very inconvenient: ingredients cannot be pasted as a list, only added one by one.
apps.whoFor: People who cook from recipes on culinary websites and want to read them without ads

apps.title: MealBoard - Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A reliable planner with good shopping list integration, but web import is unstable and the interface feels dated. Family sync needs work.
apps.loved: Everything in one place: recipes, meal plan, and an automatically generated shopping list.
apps.weak: Import from certain sites fails or needs manual correction after parsing.
apps.whoFor: People who plan meals for the week and want an automatic grocery list

apps.title: SuperCook Recipe By Ingredient
apps.verdict: SuperCook solves a unique problem: it finds recipes based on what you already have at home. The concept works and is genuinely useful, but the app is technically unstable — recipes open to a white screen and favorites do not save.
apps.loved: Finds dishes from whatever is already in the fridge, saving time and reducing food waste.
apps.weak: Ingredient-based search works, but opening a recipe often leads to a third-party site or hangs.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to cook from what they have without extra shopping

quotes.text: Having my pantry made into a menu helps reduce waste and takes some mental load off!

For example, they have one option for canned tomatoes. They don't give you the choice to differentiate between diced and crushed. If I've got crushed tomatoes that I want to use, I have to search through a bunch of recipes that require diced to find the one that uses crushed.

This app is headed in the right direction. What I love: the simplicity of adding the ingredients I have & knowing every recipe I see, I can make. No over complicated shopping lists & meal plans. Makes figuring out what to eat more fun & give flexibility to buy something on sale at the grocery store.

apps.title: KetoDiet: Fasting & Meal Plans
apps.verdict: A solid keto base with recipes, a macro tracker, and a mood journal. Inflexibility with measurement units and gaps in the US food database reduce convenience.
apps.loved: A large keto recipe library with macros and a built-in daily tracker.
apps.weak: Measurement units are rigid and minimum serving sizes cannot be adjusted to match real portion sizes.
apps.whoFor: People following keto or low-carb eating who want one place for recipes and tracking

apps.title: Mealime Meal Plans & Recipes
apps.verdict: Mealime handles meal planning and automatic shopping lists well, but since late 2025 new recipes have stopped appearing and updates have nearly ceased. The app is losing its audience because of content stagnation, not a weak core mechanic.
apps.loved: A smart meal plan that assembles the shopping list without any extra effort; recipes are easy for beginners.
apps.weak: The recipe catalog has not been updated in over six months, and you cannot search your own recipes by name inside the planner.
apps.whoFor: Families who want to cook to a plan without the hassle

quotes.text: I love this app for the ease of making my grocery list and the recipes are great

I have used this app for years. I have never heard a single built in recipe. It's just not what I wanted the app for. I'm very frustrated that I cannot search my own recipes by Name when building a menu???? This is such a basic thing??????

Haven't had the will or brainpower to cook more than bare minimum for survival for while now. This was so easy. I had food for the entire week Sunday-Sunday and actually had solid meals. My grocery budget increased a bit but there were not any wasted ingredients.

A meal plan/recipe app that DOESN'T show the calories? Even worse is they are withholding the caloric information to force you into PAYING to see this info? Why can't there be any helpful free options for a meal planning app, this is so frustrating.
Definitely love the app and it has made meal prep so much easier. I would give Mealime 5 stars if they came out with a kid-friendly category.

apps.title: Cooklist: Pantry Meals Recipes
apps.verdict: A strong concept — scanning a receipt and cooking from what is already in the pantry. But store sync is unstable and social media import breaks periodically.
apps.loved: Scanning a paper receipt fills the pantry in seconds and immediately suggests recipes from what you have at home.
apps.weak: Store connections drop on their own and do not reconnect for months without manual intervention.
apps.whoFor: Families who want to cook from pantry stock

quotes.text: Why am I paying for your app if half of your features that you advertise do not work? My Amazon has not been connecting to my app for the past 3 months. I also keep getting errors for when I import from Instagram.

I had accidentally paid for an annual membership. I was a little bit disappointed at the purchase because I didn't monitor it. But I will be renewing my annual subscription because this app is absolutely amazing. I have scanned the items in my refrigerator freezer and pantry and it makes a list for...

I love how easy it is to import recipes from other places, organizing my pantry, shopping list and the recipe selection options. The only things I would like to eventually see is the Meal plan section auto creating plans for me from using my recipes collection.

apps.title: Spillt: Recipe & Meal Plan App
apps.verdict: The only genuinely free app in the category with a social angle: save recipes from the web, build a shopping list, and discover new dishes. Ads in the free version interrupt the cooking workflow, and the app crashes occasionally.
apps.loved: Free with no hidden subscription, and it combines recipes from multiple sources into one shopping list.
apps.weak: Aggressive ads cover the interface and make it hard to follow recipe steps.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants a free recipe planner with a social feed and no subscription

apps.title: Caveman Feast - Paleo Recipes
apps.verdict: A high-quality paleo recipe collection with beautiful photos, dynamic serving recalculation, and an automatic shopping list sorted by store aisle. Prep times in recipes are often understated, and some recipes are not strictly paleo.
apps.loved: The ingredient list recalculates instantly when you change the serving count.
apps.weak: No nutritional info or macro profile for recipes, which matters on a paleo diet.
apps.whoFor: People following paleo who want inspiration for new dishes

apps.title: Kitchen Stories Easy Recipes
apps.verdict: Kitchen Stories was a strong editorial app with video recipes, but after a series of updates the videos disappeared, saved recipes break, and users are pushed toward a paid upgrade. The content is good, but the product is degrading.
apps.loved: Varied and inventive recipes with polished presentation; the cooking mode is easy to use.
apps.weak: Saved recipes can become locked after an update without warning; video instructions have disappeared.
apps.whoFor: Culinary enthusiasts willing to tolerate instability

apps.title: Stashcook: Recipe Keeper
apps.verdict: The best tool for saving recipes from social media: Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook posts are parsed into structured recipes. However, the app goes down periodically and family sharing requires a separate subscription.
apps.loved: Flawless saving of recipes from social media videos and posts with automatic ingredient parsing.
apps.weak: Family use is not accommodated: a second person must pay a separate subscription.
apps.whoFor: People who actively save recipes from TikTok and Instagram and want quick access to them

apps.title: Meal Planner & Weekly Menu
apps.verdict: A visually appealing meal planner with straightforward dish entry and a convenient shopping list. The main gap: ingredients are not automatically transferred to the list when a recipe is added to the calendar, and planning multiple weeks costs money.
apps.loved: Beautiful design and simple dish entry make using the app a daily habit.
apps.weak: Collaborative plan editing is not available for families — only view access via a shared link.
apps.whoFor: Someone who wants to plan meals visually without complexity

apps.title: Tasty: Recipes, Cooking Videos
apps.verdict: Video recipes focused on simplicity and visual appeal from BuzzFeed. The strong point is that the video format lowers the barrier to cooking, but cross-device sync does not work, dietary filters ignore allergens, and sessions do not persist between launches.
apps.loved: Video instructions make even unfamiliar dishes approachable and take the fear out of the kitchen.
apps.weak: Dietary filters do not actually work: the app continues showing recipes that contain specified allergens.
apps.whoFor: Cooking beginners who need video format instead of written instructions

quotes.text: I have to log in every time I open this app which is very frustrating. The app also refreshes to the home page almost every time I navigate away from it. I have to find and reopen the recipe I was using multiple times while I'm cooking and it's driving me cra...
This concept sounds great but if my wife and I can't log into a synced account for meal planning then what's the point? I don't see email log in as an option.
I put my lactose free and no peanut butter for can't have and it still kept giving me nothing but recipes with them in it. It was kinda frustrating.

I've had this app for about 6 months now and one day the app wouldn't open. I just got a blue screen and it froze. I uninstalled the app and reinstalled it but when I logged back in, I had NONE of my recipes I'd saved and cooked.

apps.title: CookBook - Recipe Keeper
apps.verdict: Before version 3.0 it was one of the best recipe managers, but the redesign broke familiar workflows and introduced instability. Social media import is still convenient; everything else has degraded.
apps.loved: URL import and Instagram recipe saving work instantly and accurately.
apps.weak: After the major update, navigation became more confusing and the shopping list is unreliable.
apps.whoFor: People who frequently save recipes from the web and can tolerate instability

apps.title: EatWise - Meal Reminder
apps.verdict: A clean meal-reminder timer for people who forget to eat. It does one thing well, but Apple Watch notifications do not work properly and stability drops after updates.
apps.loved: Simplicity and flexible meal scheduling without calorie counting or diet culture.
apps.weak: Notifications do not reach the watch and do not let you log a meal without opening the app.
apps.whoFor: People with a suppressed appetite or a packed schedule who forget to eat

apps.title: eMeals - Healthy Meal Plans
apps.verdict: eMeals conveniently connects a meal plan to online grocery ordering, but the shopping list often duplicates ingredients, recipes are criticized for lacking seasoning and variety, and the app is rough on tablet. It pushes Walmart at every launch.
apps.loved: One tap sends the shopping list directly to a partner store cart.
apps.weak: The shopping list duplicates ingredients; recipes taste flat without extra seasoning.
apps.whoFor: Busy families who want to cook on a schedule and order groceries online

quotes.text: The app will add dozens of random ingredients to the shopping list. I had 9 12 oz bags of broccoli when I needed 3. 9 bell peppers when I needed 3. The list goes on and on. It's to the point where it's completely unusable.
This is so easy, pick you plan, pick you dish, that creates a store list, check off items you have, send it to store for curbside pickup! Couldn't be easier and we like the meals I make. Well done!
We love this app. We've tried other options over the years, but come back to eMeals every time! I do wish there was a meal prep mode that would easily tell you what and how to prep in advance!
Their options are limited and most of the recipes we've tried lack taste/seasoning as is. If you have picky eaters pass on this one. Kids friendly was not tested with kids lol.
Busy working mom with a husband and two picky eater daughters. EMeals helps me plan and shop fast, easy and healthy. Going on 7+ years. Still love EMeals.

apps.title: SideСhef: Easy Cooking Recipes
apps.verdict: A good recipe library with a step-by-step cooking mode, but clipboard import is unstable, search returns irrelevant results, and a heavy Walmart tie-in frustrates part of the audience.
apps.loved: Step-by-step cooking mode with an image at each step and a large curated recipe base.
apps.weak: Search fails to find obvious dishes, and URL recipe import breaks without explanation.
apps.whoFor: People who want to cook from structured recipes with visual cues

apps.title: Meal Planner & Grocery List
apps.verdict: A simple planner with fast recipe import and a basic shopping list, but cross-device sync fails and recipes sometimes disappear from the dropdown. It works for those who need the bare minimum.
apps.loved: Quickly generates a shopping list from planned dishes and is easy to share with a partner.
apps.weak: The shopping list cannot be checked off item by item while walking through the store.
apps.whoFor: Couples who plan meals for the week together

apps.title: Pepper - Recipe Organizer
apps.verdict: A convenient personal recipe organizer with social media import and a link back to the original video, but there is no weekly planner, Instagram and Facebook import often freezes, and app stability declined after recent updates.
apps.loved: Saves video recipes together with a working link to the original rather than just the text.
apps.weak: No built-in weekly meal planner, even though users explicitly request exactly that feature.
apps.whoFor: Cooking enthusiasts who collect recipes from social media

quotes.text: Keeps freezing when importing from social media sites...then I have to exit out of all apps and I lose the recipe
This app has helped me find new dinner ideas but I wish it had a feature where I could plan my meals for the week. Otherwise, I can't always remember.

apps.title: 8fit Workouts & Meal Planner
apps.verdict: A combined app for short workouts and meal planning. The meal planner and ready menus have delivered real results for long-term users, but the app is frozen in development: Google sign-in is broken, Apple Health integration is absent, and no new recipes are added.
apps.loved: Ready weekly menus with simple recipes and short workouts complement each other naturally inside one app.
apps.weak: The app has not evolved in years: Google login does not work and there is no Apple Health sync.
apps.whoFor: People who want to combine short home workouts with a ready meal plan

quotes.text: My request is that the meal plans should take into account your favorite recipes when they're created. Also, if you change one meal, it would be nice to have all other instances of that meal replaced as well.

TLDR: Silent workouts are soul crushing, but the meal plans and the workout plans are very effective when followed. I used 8fit to lose 40 lbs in six months. It is an excellent app for meal planning and picking workouts.

apps.title: Fitia: Calorie Counter & Diet
apps.verdict: Fitia works as a calorie tracker with automatic meal plan generation and the core product functions. But the barcode scanner is unreliable, macros in saved recipes change on their own, and AI food recognition needs improvement.
apps.loved: Automatically builds a meal plan based on available foods and body composition goals.
apps.weak: Saved recipes change their calorie and macro values without reason; the scanner is unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Spanish-speaking users tracking their diet and weight

apps.title: Cookpad Recipes, homemade food
apps.verdict: A large global community and simple recipe publishing, but search is limited to one language and region, browsing without a subscription is awkward, and useful navigation features were removed in recent updates.
apps.loved: Sharing your own recipe with an international community and getting comments from cooks in other countries.
apps.weak: The app blocks access to recipes from other countries and languages, even though the website has no such restrictions.
apps.whoFor: Cooking enthusiasts who want to share recipes with a global community

apps.title: Recipe Notes - My Cookbook
apps.verdict: A beautiful and intuitive recipe manager with import from browser, screenshots, and cookbook photos. After an update, basic features like categories ended up behind a paywall, and some users lost recipes with no way to restore them.
apps.loved: Import works from many sources: browser, Facebook, screenshots, and book photos.
apps.weak: Cooking mode does not let you adjust the text size while actively cooking.
apps.whoFor: People who want to transfer family recipes from paper to their phone

apps.title: Home Chef: Meal Kit Delivery
apps.verdict: Home Chef earns praise for meal quality and variety, but the app itself is unstable: it freezes at launch, loses selected items when editing an order, and recipes from physical cards cannot be accessed through the app. Choosing meals for the week involves friction.
apps.loved: A complete ingredient kit with clear recipes lets you cook new dishes without a special trip for spices.
apps.weak: The app freezes at launch and does not save order changes; recipe cards from the box are inaccessible through it.
apps.whoFor: Busy households who need to cook quickly without planning their own grocery run

apps.title: My Recipe Box: Cookbook & Menu
apps.verdict: A simple recipe store with web import and automatic ingredient suggestions, but with no cross-Apple-device sync. After recent updates, users encountered intrusive ads overlaying the interface even in the paid version.
apps.loved: Fast recipe import from a website and automatic ingredient assembly for the shopping list.
apps.weak: No account login or cloud sync, so recipes are not accessible across different devices.
apps.whoFor: A single iPhone user who needs a simple personal recipe store

apps.title: Nutrition Coach: Food tracker
apps.verdict: A nutrition tracker with a meal planner and Apple Health integration. Long-term users appreciate its simplicity, but a recent update removed gram-based logging, alienating anyone who tracks macros precisely and breaking the core workflow.
apps.loved: Apple Health sync and a clean interface with no unnecessary steps work well for daily tracking.
apps.weak: After the latest update, quantities can only be entered in vague portions rather than grams, making tracking imprecise.
apps.whoFor: People just starting to monitor their diet who do not need detailed weight-based tracking

apps.title: Blue Apron: Meal Kit Delivery
apps.verdict: Blue Apron as a service delivers interesting recipes and good ingredient quality, but the app became less convenient after a redesign: current week recipes are harder to find, the planning horizon shrunk to two weeks, and step-by-step instructions during cooking got worse. Users rate the service higher than the app.
apps.loved: Recipe cards with step-by-step instructions help you master new dishes without searching for recipes.
apps.weak: After the redesign it is hard to find this week's recipes and switch between upcoming deliveries in advance.
apps.whoFor: Experienced home cooks who value variety in their meal kit delivery

apps.title: BigOven Recipes & Meal Planner
apps.verdict: BigOven has built a large recipe base over the years, but the app is now crumbling from within: cooking instructions are buried behind ads, recipe folders sort in a random order, and family sharing does not work properly.
apps.loved: A huge recipe base and the ability to maintain a personal collection with folders over many years.
apps.weak: Ads cover instructions right in the middle of cooking; folders sort in a random order.
apps.whoFor: Users with a large accumulated collection who have nowhere else to go

quotes.text: My wife does all the research.. I'm the cook. We have each other setup so we are household members and yet, we don't seem to be sharing recipes? Is this a missed opportunity? This is really the biggest feature we want/need.
I'm a paying customer and the app is unacceptable at present. My folders don't stay sorted. Sometimes they are alphabetized, sometimes not. Even back and forth. Totally random.

apps.title: RP Diet Coach & Planner
apps.verdict: A specialized macro and meal-timing coach for athletes, not a general recipe planner. After a redesign, navigation became so complex that even loyal users gave up on daily tracking.
apps.loved: A clear RP-method nutrition structure with automatic macro adjustment for training days.
apps.weak: After the redesign the interface is overwhelming: hidden features, logged data loss, and no way to quickly log a meal.
apps.whoFor: Athletes following RP periodized nutrition

apps.title: Zest: Meal Planner & Recipes
apps.verdict: Social media video recipe import works when it works, but it is unstable. Free-tier limits feel like a wall, and accounts with hundreds of recipes disappear after updates.
apps.loved: Saving recipes directly from TikTok and Instagram with automatic ingredient extraction.
apps.weak: Serving scaling is complicated and changing the number of guests requires too many steps.
apps.whoFor: Fans of culinary social content who want to collect recipes in one place

quotes.text: I liked this app because you can import videos from TikTok and ig but it doesn't work. I followed the steps exactly and later when I opened the app to see the recipes I imported, nothing was there. Super disappointed.
The recipe was really hard to follow and not worth it. It made changing the serving amount very difficult and tedious.

After the new update the app not only logged me out but seems to have deleted my account entirely. No matter what sign in method I try it's starting as a new account, even though I have over 200 recipes saved. I can't find any support line to contact.

apps.title: The Recipe Box To Go
apps.verdict: A convenient local recipe store with 15 years of history, but sync between iPhone and iPad has been broken for a long time, and an iOS 26 update wiped data for some users. Recipe entry and viewing work well as long as the data is still there.
apps.loved: Simple and fast entry of your own recipes with everything stored in one place.
apps.weak: Transferring recipes between devices via Bluetooth or local network is unreliable and often fails entirely.
apps.whoFor: Someone who prefers to keep personal recipes on a single device without cloud storage

apps.title: Whisk: Recipe Keeper & Planner
apps.verdict: The core idea is good: save a TikTok or Instagram link and get a step-by-step recipe with a shopping list. In practice, import freezes or fails every other attempt, and some users lost all their data after an update.
apps.loved: The only app that can parse recipes from TikTok and Instagram videos without manual entry.
apps.weak: No categories or folders for recipes; everything piles into one unorganized list.
apps.whoFor: People who collect recipes from short-form video

apps.title: Oh She Glows
apps.verdict: Oh She Glows offers quality vegan recipes with beautiful photos, but the app has not been updated in a long time, the content is frozen, and it is technically unstable — recipes sometimes fail to load at all.
apps.loved: The recipes taste good even for non-vegans; the presentation is attractive and navigation is simple.
apps.weak: No shopping list, no planner, and content has not been updated in over a year.
apps.whoFor: Vegans familiar with the blog who want the recipes available offline

apps.title: Recipe Gallery - Cook Book
apps.verdict: A simple recipe organizer with convenient browser and camera saving, but a widespread problem with loading recipes from iCloud makes the app unreliable for daily kitchen use.
apps.loved: One-tap import from any website and OCR of cookbook pages directly from the camera.
apps.weak: iCloud recipes stop opening and the app must be relaunched multiple times in the middle of cooking.
apps.whoFor: People who want to store a recipe collection from multiple sources

apps.title: Calo - كالو
apps.verdict: This is a ready meal delivery service with a companion app, not a recipe planner. Reviews are primarily about logistics and food quality rather than planning features. The companion app is unstable.
apps.loved: Fast delivery of ready healthy meals with a personalized diet option.
apps.weak: The menu repeats too often and variety does not match what is advertised.
apps.whoFor: Residents of UAE and Qatar ordering ready diet meals with delivery

apps.title: Menu Planner
apps.verdict: A veteran meal planner with a long history that is now running without support: printing crashes the app, barcode scanning finds nothing, and cross-device sync is unreliable. The core manual meal planning works, but everything around it is falling apart.
apps.loved: Flexible manual meal planning with grocery budgeting and custom categories.
apps.weak: Recipe import from websites is broken, and an unmaintained app is gradually losing iOS compatibility.
apps.whoFor: A longtime fan of the app who has nowhere else to go

apps.title: Gronda: Recipes for Chefs
apps.verdict: Content from real professional chefs at a high level, but search and tags are poorly implemented, video lessons cannot be saved with progress, and the app becomes very slow after extended use.
apps.loved: Techniques and recipes from working chefs that you cannot find on mainstream cooking platforms.
apps.weak: Search and tags work erratically: there is no way to filter free content from paid or find recipes by technique.
apps.whoFor: Professional chefs and culinary school students

apps.title: Noom Weight Loss, Food Tracker
apps.verdict: A weight-loss app with coaching and nutrition tracking that is only tangentially related to recipes and meal planning. The bulk of reviews document constant loading failures, intrusive gamification with virtual seeds, and a bloated interface after updates.
apps.loved: When it works without crashes, it genuinely helps with weight loss through a psychological approach and calorie tracking.
apps.weak: The interface is overloaded with animations and game mechanics that get in the way of quickly logging a meal.
apps.whoFor: People who want structured weight-loss coaching, not just recipes

apps.title: CHEF iQ
apps.verdict: CHEF iQ is aimed at controlling a smart thermometer and connected devices, not meal planning. Recipes in the app are tied to the hardware and cover a narrow range of scenarios. After a redesign the interface got worse and device connection is unstable.
apps.loved: Precise temperature control with flip prompts makes grilling predictable.
apps.weak: After the update the interface became more complex; recipes are limited to compatible equipment and do not cover regular cooking.
apps.whoFor: Owners of CHEF iQ smart thermometers who need cooking temperature control

apps.title: RecipeBox - Save Your Recipes!
apps.verdict: RecipeBox worked well as a personal recipe archive with web import, but after monetization the product degraded: intrusive Walmart ads appear on every screen transition, and import now saves only a link instead of the actual content.
apps.loved: One-click recipe import from the web and convenient manual organization by category.
apps.weak: Import increasingly saves only a link rather than the recipe itself, making the collection dependent on third-party sites.
apps.whoFor: Anyone who wants to store recipes in one place without planning features

apps.title: Marley Spoon
apps.verdict: Good, varied recipes every week, but this is a companion app to a physical delivery service where the real problems are spoiled ingredients and incomplete boxes. The iPad app does not rotate to landscape.
apps.loved: The weekly recipe rotation genuinely does not repeat, which even critical users appreciate.
apps.weak: The step-by-step cooking mode breaks periodically, and the iPad app only works in portrait orientation.
apps.whoFor: Marley Spoon subscribers who need a digital recipe card

apps.title: Dinnerly: Meal Kit
apps.verdict: The app as a meal kit interface is reasonably convenient, but the Start Cooking button stopped working after an update, making step-by-step mode inaccessible. The core product experience issue lies outside the app: wrong and spoiled ingredients in the box.
apps.loved: A wide selection of vegetarian and family recipes with clear step-by-step instructions.
apps.weak: The Start Cooking button stopped working after an update; step-by-step mode is unavailable.
apps.whoFor: Busy families who need a ready ingredient kit with simple recipes

quotes.text: Since the last update, the "Start Cooking" button no longer works - so no step by step for the recipe. You can view the whole recipe at once but that view won't keep your phone display on and it's eas...
I love this meal delivery service! What I love most is that almost all of the recipes have kid-friendly ingredients and are "normal" meals that my kids won't turn their nose up at.

apps.title: Real Plans - Meal Planner
apps.verdict: Automatic meal planning that works for Whole30 and AIP, but the app runs slowly, allergen filters are unreliable, and the algorithm generates repetitive menus without enough variety.
apps.loved: Automatically assembles a plan and grocery list for the chosen dietary protocol.
apps.weak: The algorithm cycles through the same recipes repeatedly; menu variety is extremely limited.
apps.whoFor: People doing Whole30 or AIP who want a ready plan without choosing meals themselves

apps.title: Mediterranean Diet & Meal Plan
apps.verdict: The app offers a simple daily meal plan without frills, but that is where the positives end. There are no macros, the meal-swap filter does not work by meal type, and the shopping list deletes unchecked items.
apps.loved: A clear daily meal schedule with no extra screens or decisions required.
apps.weak: No diet customization: you cannot swap a dish by meal type or save a recipe you like without adding it to the plan.
apps.whoFor: A beginner to Mediterranean eating who needs the simplest possible starting point

apps.title: Green Chef: Healthy Meal Kits
apps.verdict: Green Chef is a meal kit delivery service, not a recipe app. The app itself is basic, and the key user pain points are navigation through the menu and the absence of a favorites filter.
apps.loved: Recipes are clear and quick to follow; the food is good according to users who actually got to the kitchen.
apps.weak: No persistent diet filter; there is no normal way to find a liked dish again later.
apps.whoFor: Green Chef service customers, not for independent meal planning

apps.title: HelloFresh: Meal Kit & Recipes
apps.verdict: A companion app to a meal kit delivery service. The culinary content itself is good, but the app chronically fails: it does not save meal selections, sends random menus, ignores allergens, and crashes regularly after updates.
apps.loved: Step-by-step instructions help you cook dishes that used to feel too difficult.
apps.weak: Weekly meal selections are not saved and the app sends random menus instead of the ones you chose.
apps.whoFor: HelloFresh subscribers who need to manage their orders, not people looking for recipes

quotes.text: I love hello fresh, I use it weekly for my dinners and I love the cookbook tab. That being said, it would be so helpful if there was a cooking mode setting so my phone doesn't...

The app was tweaking out and didn't save my selection, I guess. I distinctly remember what I had selected and it was nothing seafood related since I'm highly allergic to it. I even put an add on for the meal that I did select. Yet they sent me a shrimp bowl.

apps.title: HitMeal－Calorie & Food Tracker
apps.verdict: HitMeal presents itself as a calorie tracker rather than a recipe planner: the barcode scanner is unreliable, there is no cross-device sync, and meal planning features are minimal. As a recipe and meal planning tool it is weaker than competitors.
apps.loved: A simple interface for starting out with calorie and macro tracking with no learning curve.
apps.weak: The barcode scanner is unreliable; data does not sync between phone and tablet.
apps.whoFor: Calorie-counting beginners who do not need a full meal planner

apps.title: Epicurious
apps.verdict: A recipe library from Condé Nast with content from Bon Appétit and other publications. The recipes are good quality, but the app regularly freezes at launch, fails to open for a large share of users, dietary filters do not work, and saved recipe organization is entirely absent.
apps.loved: High-quality editorial content from Bon Appétit with useful user comments beneath each recipe.
apps.weak: No folders or search within saved recipes — a long flat list with no structure is unusable.
apps.whoFor: Condé Nast subscribers who want access to Bon Appétit content

quotes.text: Absolutely love this app i just wish the dietary preferences tab was working. I cant have pork and every third recipe has pork in it. And my partner doesnt like mushrooms and the other third of the recipes have those in it.

For $5/month it should be way better. There is no ability to create folders for saved recipes. They are only available by date of save. So if I want that first soup recipe, I have to scroll thru so many recipes. There is no search saved recipes capability either.

apps.title: Keto Diet App & Recipes
apps.verdict: The app offers a keto recipe collection, but saved favorites do not persist between sessions, the interface is unstable, and a full meal planner is effectively absent. Technical problems substantially undercut the value of the content.
apps.loved: A wide selection of keto recipes with clear instructions that helps beginners get started on the diet.
apps.weak: Saved recipes reset after closing the app; the meal planning feature is almost completely absent.
apps.whoFor: People just starting keto who need ready recipes to get going

quotes.text: The app seems thorough and that it has a lot of good info, but it has one bug I've found: saving things to your cookbook/favorites doesn't work. It will add them, but they will be removed the next day. I have verified this over the course of two days.

apps.title: Diet Plan: Smart Meal Planner
apps.verdict: Meal plans without detailed recipes and with questionable dish compositions; functionality is limited. A significant share of five-star reviews was obtained through incentivization.
apps.loved: Simple onboarding with personalization to your goal and lifestyle.
apps.weak: Meal plans without step-by-step recipes or proper proportions; date navigation is awkward.
apps.whoFor: Practically no one who actually wants to cook to a plan

apps.title: Anova Culinary
apps.verdict: Anova Culinary functions as sous vide device control; the recipe and guide section became unstable after recent updates. For most users the Guides section crashes on every open, and reconnecting the device is required every session.
apps.loved: Remote start and temperature monitoring for sous vide via the phone works accurately with a stable connection.
apps.weak: The guides and recipes section crashes on every open; device reconnection is required at every session.
apps.whoFor: Anova circulator owners who need temperature control without recipe planning

apps.title: Eatr: Tasty Cooking Recipes
apps.verdict: The app blocks access to its own recipes with a long, unskippable onboarding sequence, and most positive reviews are empty. Recipes are decent in concept but do not scale to a real number of servings.
apps.loved: A visually clean interface and a reasonable selection of quick recipes for those who actually reach the content.
apps.weak: Recipes do not show a serving count and cannot be scaled, so there is no way to adapt them to a real number of people.
apps.whoFor: Hard to recommend to anyone in the current state

quotes.text: I tried this for the recipes, and they good, but they're all over the place. Some are recipes for several people, others for one. They're not scalable, and they don't tell you how many servings you're making. Basically useless.

apps.title: Healthy CrockPot Recipes
apps.verdict: A slow cooker recipe collection with an extremely unreliable access system: users pay for premium and cannot open the recipes. There is no meaningful meal planning or shopping list functionality.
apps.loved: Some slow cooker recipes are practical and work for busy parents.
apps.weak: Category navigation loses your position in the list and randomly jumps to a different part of the catalog.
apps.whoFor: Slow cooker owners who need a basic recipe set without extra features

apps.title: Recipe Keeper & Saver - Recify
apps.verdict: The app regularly loses all saved recipes after updates or re-login, and import is unreliable and often drops partway through to system settings. The product is too raw and unreliable to serve as a recipe store.
apps.loved: The idea of importing recipes directly from Instagram and TikTok via the share sheet is appealing.
apps.weak: Recipes disappear after an app update or plan change; there is no backup option.

apps.title: Perfect Body - Meal planner
apps.verdict: The app offers a limited recipe set and does not allow adding your own dishes. There is almost no product value; users cannot properly plan meals or maintain their own diet.
apps.loved: A few ready recipes look appealing and prompt users to start thinking about healthy eating.
apps.weak: You cannot add your own dish to the plan; only recipes from the app's built-in library are allowed.
apps.whoFor: Beginners who need ready meal ideas without any flexibility

apps.title: 30 Day Whole Foods Meal Plan
apps.verdict: The app does not open for most users, support is silent, and the recipes do not follow the spirit of Whole30. There is almost no functional meal planning here.
apps.loved: A few users note tasty and simple recipes when the app actually works.
apps.weak: No way to add sides or accompaniments to dishes; recipes do not combine into a complete meal.
apps.whoFor: Not recommended to anyone in the current state

apps.title: CookEasy – Recipe Finder
apps.verdict: The app impersonates the well-known Allrecipes website, charges money, and does not open any recipes. Actual Allrecipes representatives publicly confirmed they have no connection to this app.
apps.loved: Users who got a refund through Apple at least managed to resolve the issue through store support.
apps.weak: Recipe search does not work at all; there is almost no content inside.
apps.whoFor: No one
